gaps.text: ZCode sessions get mid-session injection when the working directory changes
gaps.details: Evidence: README, verbatim — 'Known limitations, stated bluntly: no param trigger — ZCode's PreToolUse hook sees tool arguments and could carry a mid-session injection, but its stdout-to-context path is unproven, so the adapter ships without one (like Claude Code).' The Hermes adapter already has one: each user turn scans new tool-call parameters (terminal command+workdir, read_file/write_file/patch/search_files path). Done = ZCode gets mid-session coverage on a proven stdout-to-context path, or the limitation is retired with the reason recorded.

gaps.text: An interrupted session still leaves a session record
gaps.details: Evidence: README — 'no true close hook: a session interrupted with SIGINT/SIGTERM — or a terminal closed — writes no record, because Stop only steers at a turn boundary and nothing fires at process exit.' So session-end records miss exactly the aborted sessions worth knowing about. Done = a session killed by signal or a closed terminal leaves a record (summary: null is honest and fine) for every adapter that can host such a hook.

gaps.text: deep-horizon is installable from the npm registry
gaps.details: Re-tracks the want the Sep-11 npm-release close dropped while registry.npmjs.org still 404s. A registry tarball ships dist/ as packed and never runs prepare on the user's machine, so this also erases the npm-12 install-scripts friction documented in Install. Done = npm install -g deep-horizon works from the registry.

about: A CLI plus per-harness adapters that keep a project's aim — one about line, up to 5 gaps — in front of every agent session, from one shared .horizon store
